[ASSISTANT_SAID] Strategies for setting healthy boundaries when dealing with a toxic partner include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Identify and acknowledge the problem: Recognize and accept that the relationship is toxic and take responsibility for your own feelings and actions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Clearly communicate your boundaries: Be clear and concise when communicating your boundaries to your partner. Use “I” statements and avoid blaming or attacking language.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Be consistent: Stick to your boundaries and enforce them consistently. This will show your partner that you’re serious about your boundaries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Seek support: Reach out to friends, family, or a therapist to help you work through your feelings and to gain support in setting and enforcing your boundaries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Take care of yourself: Make sure to prioritize self-care and take time for yourself to relax, reflect, and recharge.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Practice compassion and forgiveness: Toxic behaviors often stem from past trauma or unmet needs. Try to practice empathy and understanding for your partner, but also remember to prioritize your own well-being.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Strategies for dealing with guilt-tripping include:

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Don't engage in arguments: Try not to engage in arguments or get defensive.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Stick to your boundaries: Be firm and consistent with your boundaries, even if your partner tries to make you feel guilty.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use "I" statements: Express how their behavior is affecting you using "I" statements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Seek support: Consider reaching out to a trusted friend or therapist for support and guidance.
